answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake when a randomly audited contribution proves fraudulent. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital behind every fake account, while honest agents recover their deposits; creating identities alone no longer buys influence. The stake can be ferrous in a tokenized sense, not iron: a plume of linked accounts still faces the same per-identity cost, like rows in an orchard.
